title: Choose the visual world
question: The homepage is unequal sheets you can open, with a bar on the top and a bar on the side. Keep the station case, take the notice board, or re-roll.

options.label: The station case
options.lineage: An Israeli bus-stop glass case, read in noon light
options.thesis: The organization is a public case: unequal sheets behind glass, and joining is the orange route you take.
options.viewport: A floating enamel header and a side route strip frame a glass case of unequal posters. The real logo sits in the header. The tallest blue sheet carries the civic sentence. A small orange ticket says הצטרפו.
options.risk: If the glass and the route strip are only decoration, it collapses into a card grid with a blue navbar.

raised.raise: Sheets keep their own mass and settle by content height, instead of stretching to one card size.
One orange is live, and it belongs only to the sheet your hand is on.
The lead sheet may break the case grid when the notice is the one that matters.
The top and side bars are the registration notches: they stay put between sheets, and only a full-page experience lifts the frame off.
The side rail is one sweep of same-height stops, and one of them sits in the orange.
The newest sheet is the darkest ink in the case. Older notices sit lighter.

options.label: The notice wall
options.lineage: The municipal notice board outside a community center
options.thesis: Belonging starts as a board you already know how to read: papers of different sizes, one orange pin on the join slip.
options.viewport: Cork fills the page. A thin top rail holds the real logo. A side index of pins names the sheets. Unequal notes pack down the board, and הצטרפו is the only orange ticket.
options.risk: Familiar. A warm board of papers is where civic homepages land, and it fails if the cork is a texture over ordinary cards.

options.label: Gravity rain
options.lineage: A garden where each cloud pulls rain on its own law
options.thesis: Each notice would fall into place by a color of gravity, and the join would be a river finding its flower.
options.viewport: Bent Hebrew baselines and sheets drifting toward colored clouds.
options.case: Loses both. Citizens of Israel do not see themselves in an impossible garden, and bent type hides the invitation.
options.kept: Sheets keep their own mass and settle by content height.

options.label: Paper menagerie
options.thesis: Turning a crank would open each notice in order, with one crimson fold for the figure in motion.
options.viewport: A procession of paper figures, the join hidden until the crank reaches it.
options.case: Loses both. A paper toy is not how this audience recognizes a movement, and the invitation waits on a crank.
options.kept: One orange is live, and it belongs only to the sheet your hand is on.

options.label: Layout desk
options.lineage: A surf-magazine layout desk where columns collide
options.thesis: The eye would assemble the page from the loudest fragment, and reading order would be earned.
options.viewport: Headlines crashing through each other, the civic sentence buried under the wreckage.
options.case: Loses both. A surf magazine is not this audience, and a page you feel before you can read fails the invitation.
options.kept: The lead sheet may break the grid when the notice is the one that matters.
options.risk: Illegible Hebrew dressed up as attitude.

options.label: Block registration
options.lineage: A woodblock print built one registered color at a time
options.thesis: The page would print in layers, outline first, and the offer would arrive on a later pull.
options.viewport: A sheet still missing its colors, the join waiting for a later impression.
options.case: Loses both. A Japanese print is not this audience’s object, and a delayed reveal hides the door.
options.kept: The bars are registration notches: they stay put, and only a full-page experience lifts the frame.

options.label: Meter bridge
options.lineage: A row of VU meters behind glass
options.thesis: Identical channels would be read as a sweep, and opening one would be beside the point.
options.viewport: A row of identical meters, none of them a page you can open.
options.case: Loses both. A recording desk is not this audience, and the grammar forbids opening a sheet.
options.kept: The side rail is one sweep of same-height stops, one of them in the orange.
options.risk: A tool for operators, not a public address.

options.label: Ink basin
options.thesis: The page would be one liquid surface, and the words would sit outside it.
options.viewport: A swirling basin with the Hebrew held in a still margin, because the surface cannot carry a sentence.
options.case: Loses both. Marbling is not this audience’s object, and a surface that cannot hold Hebrew fails the page.
options.kept: The newest sheet is the darkest ink. Older notices sit lighter.
options.risk: Atmosphere with the address exiled to the edge.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A centered invitation: the logo, the line, one blue button.
canonCard.viewport: The real logo centered, בונים תקומה ציונית beneath it, הצטרפו לתנועה as a blue button, quiet space around them.
canonCard.risk: This is the splash the project is replacing, played straight.
